subject: Vortex Labs - AZ3 mid-day partition causing 5xx/latency — urgent
messages:
From: Priya Shah <ops@vortexlabs.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: platform@vortexlabs.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: High error rates & token latency in us-west-2 AZ3 (major impact)

Maya / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp spike in 502s and per-token latency around 10:45 PT today for all traffic routed to us-west-2 AZ3. Error rates for generation calls jumped from ~0.2% to >8% and median token latency increased from ~45ms to 1.3s. This is affecting our checkout NLU flow and causing visible errors in production.

We’ve attached a small sample of RT logs and a screenshot from our dashboard. Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing an AZ-local problem? We need an ETA on mitigation or a cross-region failover plan.

Priya Shah
Platform Reliability Lead
Vortex Labs

Attachments: vortex_RT_logs_20261123.zip, 502-sample-screenshot-az3.png

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, ops@vortexlabs.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rates & token latency in us-west-2 AZ3 (major impact)

Thanks Priya — and sorry you’re hitting this. Team, looping you in for immediate triage and exec visibility. Summary: Vortex (customer, high priority) reports sudden 5xx spike + token latency in us-west-2 AZ3 beginning ~10:45 PT. Impact: user-facing checkout errors and increased error budget burn.

Immediate asks:
- Engineering: please confirm if this is AZ-local infrastructure degradation (network, routing, GPU nodes) vs. model-serving runtime behavior. If infra AZ issue, execute cross-region routing per runbook.
- SEA / Execs (Sean): need a short customer-facing timeline and approval for transient credits if we have a prolonged recovery.

Dylan / Steph, please triage and confirm actions in the next 15 minutes. I’ve attached the customer logs Priya sent.

— Maya Srinivasan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: vortex_RT_logs_20261123.zip

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: engineering-oncall@redwood.com, ops@vortexlabs.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rates & token latency in us-west-2 AZ3 (major impact)

Quick update and actions taken:
- Observed sustained queue backlog on a subset of AZ3 racks serving the us-west-2 model deployment (correlated with kernel OOMs on 3 nodes). API 5xxs match the same window as backlog spikes.
- Immediately removed the affected instance pool from the routing plane and started a staged cross-region reroute to eastus2 (preferred warm pool) to preserve session continuity. Traffic is shifting in waves (10% -> 30% -> 100%) to avoid cache cold starts; currently at ~65% shifted.
- Runbook used: cross-region-reroute-v2 (snippet attached). We are keeping a small fraction pinned to us-west-2 to allow graceful draining and KV cache warm-up for favorite customers.

Next actions:
- Complete 100% traffic shift in next ~7–12 minutes unless new errors appear.
- Collect flamegraphs / kernel traces from the affected nodes for root cause (will follow up with infra).
- Customer comms: Maya, recommend: immediate acknowledgement + ETA: "we’ve initiated an automated cross-region reroute; majority of traffic will see restored performance within ~20 minutes; we’ll follow up with a detailed postmortem."

Attachments: cross-region-reroute-runbook-v2.pdf

— Dylan Brooks
Engineering (Serving Runtime)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <ops@vortexlabs.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rates & token latency in us-west-2 AZ3 (major impact) — failover complete

Priya — quick customer-facing update.

We confirmed an AZ-local degradation in us-west-2 AZ3 and initiated an automatic cross-region reroute to eastus2. Traffic routing is complete; latency and error rates have returned to baseline for the vast majority of requests. Our team will deliver a detailed postmortem with root cause analysis and remediation steps by EOD tomorrow.

Immediate next steps for Vortex:
- We’ll offer a transient account credit to cover the impact window — Sean will confirm amount.
- We’ll share the postmortem + kernel traces once engineering finishes the RCA.
- If you want us to pin Vortex to eastus2 for the next 72 hours while we validate stability, we can coordinate that change as a temporary mitigation.

Again, apologies for the disruption. Thanks for the quick signal and patience; Dylan / infra team will follow up with technical details.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none referenced
